#2121. Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain is one of football's great talents... so why can't he get games in this struggling Celtic side?

Published: 16:18 EDT, 2 November 2026 | Updated: 18:17 EDT, 2 November 2026

How has it come to this for Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain, one of the most gifted and decorated England internationals of his generation?

Here, after all, is a midfielder whose precocious talent as a teenager at Southampton went on to earn him a full house of English trophies.

In six years with Arsenal and six with Liverpool, there was also a Champions League winner’s medal and 35 caps for his country.

And yet now, at the age of 33, he finds himself struggling to get games for a Celtic side who are a shadow of their former selves, especially in Europe.

Used only sparingly this season, the Ox was given a rare start against Falkirk yesterday, when he was preferred to Benjamin Nygren.

Celtic boss Martin O’Neill said he needed someone with experience to take care of the ball but the Englishman was substituted 65 minutes into a 2-0 defeat.

Celtic midfielder Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain was given a rare start in the defeat by Falkirk

The Englishman has made only eight appearances in Martin O'Neill's team this season

It will not have escaped Oxlade-Chamberlain’s notice that former club Besiktas are Celtic’s next opponents in the Europa League on Thursday night.

The midfielder’s recent travails can be traced back to his move to Turkey in 2023, after Liverpool deemed him surplus to requirements.

His first few months at Besiktas went well enough, but he was soon sidelined by injury, as he had frequently been at Anfield, and his career in Turkey was already on the slide.

Concerned by his fitness and his salary, Besiktas wanted to offload him but he stayed another season and found himself frozen out by manager Giovanni van Bronckhorst.

Although Ole Gunnar Solskjaer was more willing to give him opportunities, his contract was terminated in July and it wasn’t until the following February that he found another club.

That club was Celtic, so plagued by crises on and off the pitch that they were happy to secure him on a short-term deal, even if he was a little rusty.

Oxlade-Chamberlain made all the right noises, describing Celtic as the ‘perfect fit’, the kind of club whose size and expectation he was used to.

And sure enough, he scored a late winner on his debut against Livingston and helped his new team to a double, albeit the most troubled one in their long history. He then signed a one-year contract extension and spoke of looking forward to his first proper pre-season in three years.

Oxlade-Chamberlain won the Premier League and Champions League in his time at Liverpool

It hasn’t done him much good. So far, he has made only eight appearances, four of them from the start. O’Neill seems loath to rotate a midfield in which Callum McGregor is over-used.

You can’t have the world at your feet forever, but a little more game time was expected for a player who is two years younger than James Forrest.

Maybe all those injuries have caught up with him. Maybe his playing style isn’t best suited to the ageing process. In his prime, he was explosive, strong and adept at breaking the lines, whereas now the priority is to stay fit.

Or perhaps he is just another victim of the Celtic curse that befalls Premier League stars who venture north in the twilight of their careers.

From Middlesbrough’s Brazilian World Cup winner Juninho, to Arsenal greats Ian Wright and Freddie Ljungberg, there are more than a few who have come a cropper in Glasgow’s east end.

Oxlade-Chamberlain isn’t in that category, but he has work to do if his veteran stardust is to have any chance of disguising the deep-rooted problems at Celtic Park. He needs a chance, and he needs to take it… sooner rather than later.

#2120. Portsmouth must take action over 22-year-old’s League One loan as Mousinho confirms clear ‘need’: Opinion

Portsmouth signed Hayden Matthews as a highly-rated centre-back prospect in the winter of 2025. He had emerged as one to watch at Sydney FC and quickly made a good impression at Pompey too, with his performance away at Oxford United in the 2024/25 season one fondly remembered.

But, Matthews was loaned to Bradford City for the 2025/26 season after a string of injury blows and centre-back signings. Unfortunately, the 22-year-old has struggled for minutes at Valley Parade, and manager John Mousinho has stressed his need for game time.

Speaking to The News on Matthews’ situation, Mousinho said earlier in November: “He’s gone out on loan with every intention to play, but unfortunately Bradford’s (defensive) record is one of the best in the country. We’ll see what happens – they (Matthews and Josh Knight at Reading) need to play.”

Matthews is a highly promising centre-back. His time at Portsmouth has been disrupted, but there are few doubts over his potential having displayed his composure on the ball, progressive abilities in possession and knack for reading the game.

A loan to Bradford City felt ideal, allowing Matthews to play in a solid defensive setup at a level that would require him to develop his physical game. However, he didn’t get any opportunities under Graham Alexander, and his struggles have continued under Michael Duff too.

All of George Pratt, Macaulay Gillesphey, Aden Baldwin, Reece Welch and Matthew Pennington have ranked ahead of Matthews in the pecking order. Given that they have kept nine clean sheets and conceded only eight goals in 13 League One matches, it seems unlikely that the setup is changed to make way for the Pompey loan man.

Portsmouth can not allow this to continue for the entire season, and Mousinho’s words suggest they won’t. Barring a miraculous turnaround, the Championship side must take action and recall Matthews this winter.

Matthews’ Bradford City stay has not gone as hoped, and his struggle for game time may seem like a put-off for some admirers. However, the Portsmouth man is clearly a talented defender, and he has plenty of room to grow with meaningful minutes in the right setup.

It means that other League One clubs should not hesitate to move for Matthews when Pompey recall him. Ideally, he can play in a team similar to Bradford City, who prioritise a strong defensive base.

That will ensure Matthews has plenty of opportunities to develop the areas of his game he needs to focus on.

Matthews is under contract at Fratton Park until 2029, and there is still scope for him to forge a future at the Championship side. However, finding minutes to grow as a player is a must for 2027.

#2118. O'Neill is running out of road...and the heat around him could rise extremely quickly

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 15:04 EDT, 2 November 2026 | Updated: 18:18 EDT, 2 November 2026

Moments after the tin lid was placed on a truly hideous week for Celtic with a home league defeat to Rangers, Martin O’Neill uttered some words which he later came to regret.

‘I genuinely will reflect and see,’ said the Northern Irishman when asked if he would consider his future. ‘It’s a matter of whether I can help the team. The manager is supposed to be able to do that. I will look at that this week.

‘I think every single time something crops up and things don’t go so well, age plays a part. And do you know what? They might be right. I’ll be 110 in two years’ time so it might be time to wrap it up.’

That was on September 20. Despite going into the international break on the back of two losses to Rangers and a reverse at home to Ferencvaros, with a capitulation away to LASK still in the background, O’Neill, as we know, came back for more.

The trouble is that the impasse changed very little. In the seven matches since, Celtic have won three and lost three.

The running total of clean sheets now stands at one in ten. If anyone feels that dismal sequence will improve when Besiktas come to town on Thursday, you can name your price.

With the next international break coming after Kilmarnock’s visit to Parkhead on Sunday, it feels like further self-reflection is imminent and more difficult conversations are about to take place behind the scenes.

If O’Neill and the club’s directors can identify a reason to feel that an upturn in fortunes is on the horizon, they will be in the minority.

Martin O'Neill can barely look as his Celtic side lost 2-0 to Falkirk on Sunday

In terms of results and performances, this is a team which is flatlining. It takes a leap of faith to believe that a radical improvement lies just around the corner.

For many Celtic supporters, reconciling themselves with the truth of the current situation is not easy.

In his first spell in charge at the turn of the century, O’Neill transformed their club from a laughing stock into Scotland’s dominant team and a European force to be reckoned with once again.

Last season, against all the odds, the veteran twice rode to the rescue to land an unlikely league and cup double.

Those who wished that the credits would then roll on the story of the legend’s great return have spent much of this campaign watching through the cracks in their fingers.

While O’Neill has unquestionably been the latest manager to suffer through the ineptitude of those who are supposedly running the show, nor can he be granted a free pass for what his side are routinely serving up.

The triumphs of the early 2000s and last season offer little shelter from the current storm.

Taken purely in isolation, Sunday’s loss to Falkirk could have been shrugged off as one of those unfortunate days by those stood in the visitors’ section.

The Celtic manager must wish he had quit after trophy triumph at end of last season

Celtic did have more possession than the Bairns (70.2 per cent). They had more touches inside the opposition box (44 v 15). They had more corners (14 v 0). They had more shots at goal (24 v 6). Scott Bain, the former Celtic keeper, did have a fine game.

The trouble is that the affair was no anomaly. O’Neill’s side are making a habit of showing up well in the metrics which don’t win you points and showing up badly in the only statistic which matters.

Attempting to accentuate the positives in the aftermath, the manager pointed out that the side was still better off than at this stage last year.

While this is statistically true in the Premiership — 28 points now as opposed to 26 in 2025 — that’s no cause for celebration.

Celtic were also still in the League Cup 12 months back. And after three games in the Europa League, the team had four points compared to zero being on the board at the same juncture this time. The dogs in the street know this is a team which is regressing.

O’Neill’s plea for patience in the case of new players requiring time to adapt to their new environment doesn’t cut any ice.

O'Neill's legend at the club will never diminish but this term has been his most troubling

A club which welcomed 17 new faces in the summer, six of Falkirk’s outfield players on Sunday weren’t there last season — as opposed to three of the visitors. John McGlynn doesn’t seem to have the same issues getting lesser-paid individuals assimilated to his way of working.

There have been a couple of recurring themes to Celtic under O’Neill this season. With the ball, the players lack zip, imagination and penetration. Without it, they look meek and vulnerable.

Just as Dundee United did on Wednesday, McGlynn’s side repeatedly cut them open at the weekend.

The more glaring the shortcomings become, the more legitimate it is to question if the structure of the side and the tactical approach is all that it might be.

In the days when O’Neill was able to field a team containing the likes of Paul Lambert, Lubo Moravcik and Henrik Larsson, the manager didn’t have to fret about the minor details.

With his sheer presence giving a squad brimming with top-level players added psychological strength, Celtic invariably overpowered their opponents.

Cameron Carter-Vickers and Callum McGregor have both had their say on team's tactics

Evidently, that embarrassment of riches no longer exists. Is O’Neill, at 74 years of age, capable of relaying the required tactical information to a much more limited group?

Is the correct detail forthcoming from his cadre of young coaches — Shaun Maloney, Mark Fotheringham and Stephen McManus? It’s certainly a moot point.

You could be forgiven for believing that the current crop of players have reservations about their level of tactical preparedness and the structure of the side.

Also speaking after that 1-0 loss to Rangers, Cameron Carter-Vickers claimed the team ‘played a bit too random.’

For one senior player to bemoan a lack of a plan was one thing. For another to question it set the alarm bells off.

Following the 2-2 draw with United, a match which initially saw O’Neill play two centre-forwards in Camilo Duran and Callum Osmand as wingers, skipper Callum McGregor opined that ‘the players behave like a winger, or they behave like a striker.’

He added: ‘You can get away with it for a few games, but if it’s a striker playing as a winger, you are going to get that behaviour a lot of the time.’

Over the weekend, James McClean, who played under O’Neill for Ireland, reprised the theme as he promoted his new book.

Celtic ran into an inspired Falkirk team, and a superb keeper in Scott Bain on Sunday

Recalling the bemusement of the raft of English Championship players who O’Neill called up, McClean offered: ‘Martin wasn’t big on tactics.’

Whatever accusations could justifiably be levelled at the manager and his coaching staff, those who hold them solely responsible for the current malaise are small in number.

Having got away with it — as Celtic did last season — a forward-thinking football club wouldn’t have gone back to the well by asking a septuagenarian to go again.

Not only did the Parkhead hierarchy predictably show a lack of vision by failing to appoint a younger manager with fresh ideas, they, again, failed O’Neill in the transfer market.

The selling of Arne Engels to West Ham on the eve of the season-defining clash with LASK was the latest dereliction of duty.

The six players signed in the final hours of the window — five of them loans — was the equivalent of a dash down the bargain aisle at closing time on Christmas Eve.

The board are still main target of fans, but O'Neill can't escape all the blame for poor displays on pitch

O’Neill, notably, hasn’t gone public with his dismay at the hand he was dealt in the manner in which his predecessor, Brendan Rodgers, did. But if he’s happy to toe the party line, the responsibility for a failing football team falls squarely on his shoulders.

The heat around him could rise extremely quickly. Two years after making a commendable impact in the Champions League under Rodgers, by the end of this week, an emaciated squad could find itself propping up the 36-team Europa League table.

Whether that transpires or not, the level of acrimony which constantly surrounds the club these days seems set to increase.

For O’Neill, with each passing week, a return to the comfort of a radio studio must hold greater appeal.

#2117. Celtic's record transfer handed surprising ‘doesn’t matter’ goals verdict

Kasper Hogh has been told he can still have a major impact at Celtic even if the goals don’t start flowing.

Riseth watched the Danish frontman flourish at Bodo/Glimt and feels his physical presence can be used to create opportunities for the players around him. He said: “Hogh is a big, strong target man. When he played for Bodo, they played a different style that worked for him. [SunSport]

#2116. Sheffield Wednesday transfer update emerges as Dave Challinor faces tricky situation

Sheffield Wednesday remain in discussions with the EFL over what they can do in the January window, although it seems unlikely Dave Challinor will be in a position to make major changes to the squad.

It was a remarkably hectic summer for the Owls after Arise Capital Partners completed their takeover of the club at the end of the previous campaign.

A major squad overhaul followed, but Wednesday were under EFL restrictions in terms of what they could do, so the squad was packed out with loan signings and free transfers.

Nevertheless, they still boast a lot of quality by League One standards, but an inconsistent start to the season meant Henrik Pedersen paid the price as he lost his job.

The Yorkshire outfit moved quickly to bring in Dave Challinor as his successor, and the former Stockport boss is preparing for his first game in charge at Oldham on Sunday in the FA Cup.

Whilst he will be keen on a cup run, the league will be the priority, and Challinor will hope to take Wednesday back to the Championship at the first attempt.

In normal circumstances, the new boss would also have one eye on the January window, where he may want to make a few tweaks to the group.

Yet, as outlined above, the situation at Wednesday is different due to the restrictions, and the Sheffield Star has stated that the club are ‘close to the limit’ in terms of what they can spend.

FLW looks at who entertains the most, and the least, in League One

And, speaking to the same outlet, sporting director Simon Wilson admitted they still don’t know exactly how they will be able to back Challinor in the New Year.

“We’re not 100 per cent sure exactly what it is. We’re constantly in dialogue with the league around the rules and the limitations. We obviously have the ability to change the squad, as anyone does. The window is open and business can be done.

“At this moment in time, Dave has just come into the building, he needs a bit of time to assess the squad and get a feel for which players are going to be the most useful and where we have areas of need. Then we’ll work into the window from that point.”

Obviously, this is not ideal for Wednesday, as most clubs will already be drawing up plans for January, and whilst the Owls may have players in mind, they still don’t know who they can bring in.

#2115. Nicky Butt tears into 'bluffer' and 'cheat' Lisandro Martinez after his red card against Chelsea - and insists he should be the first player on Man United's chopping block in January

By HARRY BAMFORTH, LIVE SPORTS COVERAGE REPORTER

Published: 15:53 EDT, 2 November 2026 | Updated: 03:05 EDT, 3 November 2026

Former Manchester United midfielder Nicky Butt has ripped into Lisandro Martinez following the defender's red card at Chelsea on Saturday.

The United centre-back was given his marching orders in the second half of the 2-0 defeat at Stamford Bridge for picking up two yellow cards in the space of 82 seconds.

The second of those cards came when Martinez flung an arm into the face of Wesley Fofana in the penalty box with the crucial game hanging in the balance. Cole Palmer ultimately squeezed the spot kick past Senne Lammens to secure three points for the Blues.

Martinez has been solely blamed by many for the defeat and Nicky Butt, who has previously criticised the Argentine, ripped into the 28-year-old on Piers Morgan's show Football Uncensored, dubbing him a 'cheat' for elbowing Fofana.

'Performance-wise, he's been lacking so much,' Butt said. 'And again, I was never the best player. I know my level, I know I had a lot of bad games, but one thing I did every time I went out was run myself into the ground. He threw it in the other day.

'He threw it in with that elbow because that was the most obvious thing anybody could do. And the reason he did it is because he's not strong enough to defend properly.'

Nicky Butt has hit out at Man United defender Lisandro Martinez for getting sent off at Chelsea

Butt called Martinez a 'bluffer' and a 'cheat' during a near three-minute-rant on the player

Martinez has hit the headlines more than once in the last month after he hit out at United's Director of Football Jason Wilcox for the club's lack of business, following a 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid in the Champions League.

However, Butt, who was a part of United's famous 1999 treble-winning team, has claimed that if Martinez made those comments as part of former squads, he would have come in for harsh treatment.

'He has got the audacity to go out onto an interview and s**g off the powers that be about buying players when he is not even playing well himself. And if they were going to spend money on players, he'd [ought to] be careful because he's the first one they'd replace.'

He added: 'If it was back in my day, he would have completely had his head ripped off. Everyone would have said, "Who do you think you are talking about me like that with the performances you're putting in?". And even if you're European Player of the Year, you still don't talk like that about your team-mates.

'He has now gone from - I have no idea why - someone that the fans loved to someone the fans loathe and want out of their football club.'

It is not the first time Butt has had his say on Martinez, with the pair embroiled in a feud earlier this year. Back in January, Martinez hit back at comments made by Paul Scholes and Butt mocking his size, and dared the former United duo to repeat them to his face.

Martinez was given his marching orders and conceded a penalty after striking Wesley Fofana's face during a 2-0 defeat at Stamford Bridge

The Argentine told them they can come 'to my house' and 11 months on Butt started his near-three-minute rant by referencing the back and forth.

'That lad's a bluffer, full stop,' Butt said. The Butcher his nickname is. With him, he called out my mate; it was probably my fault because I said something tongue-in-cheek on a podcast.

'It was like, "Haaland would pick up and carry him". It was tongue-in-cheek, even though Solanke did it one week ago.

'He's come out and called out a player who has won 11 Premier Leagues for Manchester United, and played for god knows how many years, about you come and see me and knock on my front door.

'You can't say anything about these players because they get all touchy with it.'

#2114. James Bree incident in West Brom v Southampton match sparks reaction

Southampton full-back James Bree has sparked a strong reaction on social media following his side's 1-1 draw with West Bromwich Albion on Tuesday night.

With the scores level in B71 after Samuel Edozie equalised early in the second period following Isaac Price's first-half opener, it has been debated whether the Saints defender successfully deceived referee, Josh Smith, who stopped the game for a head injury.

Both West Brom and Southampton have started the Championship season in impressive form, with Tonda Eckert's side still sitting amongst the division's early pacesetters despite being deducted four points due to the Spygate scandal.

Those who are a part of the South Coast club have, this season, been playing the role of pantomime villains, and that was certainly the case at The Hawthorns for those backing the hosts, who are now unbeaten in six successive matches.

Who are the biggest wind-up specialists in the EFL Championship right now? Football League World takes a deep dive...

In what was a pulsating encounter, it is fair to say that Albion were more than deserving of their half-time lead, with Saints' attack leaving Max O'Leary untroubled, before Edozie's 53rd-minute leveller certainly gave Eckert's side a fresh impetus.

West Brom still showed signs that they could take all three points, and after a spell of attacking promise, Bree was seen on the ground without movement, leaving Smith to stop the game, although the Southampton physios were swiftly waved away by the full-back.

Asked about the incident post-match, Morrison stated: "I think, because the pressure was coming from us, he tried to stop the game.

Asked whether Bree should have face further punishment, the Baggies boss added: "We've asked for consistency, so let's hope it comes."

West Brom, of course, saw Aune Heggebo banned for two matches for the deception of a match official in August after his handballed goal on the opening day against Norwich City, which was the first time a player had been banned for such wrongdoing in English football.

As such, Baggies fans are calling for Bree to face a similar punishment.

"Faking head injuries is becoming all too common and requires stronger action from officials. If staying down holding your head resulted in an automatic 3 minutes off the pitch while checked over by medics, I suspect we’ll suddenly see a lot less of it," was the opinion of one Albion fan.

Another Baggies supporter wrote: "Disgraceful behaviour, so obvious what he was doing before ref blew his whistle & then waved his hands to say he don’t need any medical attention so he don’t go off. Ref was very poor all night tho imo. Standard EFL ref."

West Brom and Southampton fans, what are your thoughts on the incident? Comment below!

"Absolutely appalling behaviour - so clear and obvious - should have been booked and EFL need to take immediate action for the credibility of football," was another strong verdict on the matter.

"It shouldn’t be done, but it literally happens in every game of professional football," another comment read.

There is, ultimately, no proof that the Baggies would have definitely restored their advantage, but given the punishment which Heggebo received two months ago, the stance of those associated with the West Midlands club is hardly a surprise.

Bree's decision to go down isn't the only incident which has been heavily criticised in recent days too, with Liverpool legend, Jamie Carragher, slamming Alexis Mac Allister's decision to 'feign' injury after the Argentinian midfielder brushed heads with Arsenal's Noni Madueke in the Gunners' 1-0 win at Anfield.

Five players, five careers. Name them from the clubs they played for.

Each day there are five current or former EFL players to identify. For each one you’ll see their senior clubs in the order they played for them. Loan spells are left out.

You get four guesses per player. Every wrong guess unlocks a clue: first their position, then their nationality, then their initials.

Get it first time for 4 points, then 3, 2 and 1. The best possible score is 20. A new set of players arrives at midnight.

At present, though, it remains to be seen what action, if any, will be taken.

Match officials have been confirmed for Celtic’s upcoming clashes with Besiktas and Kilmarnock.

Celtic face the Turkish side at Celtic Park in the Europa League before returning to Premiership duty against Kilmarnock in Glasgow.

German referee Sascha Stegemann will take charge of Celtic’s meeting with Besiktas. He will be assisted by fellow Germans Christof Gunsch and Marco Achmuller, with Martin Petersen appointed as the fourth official. Benjamin Brand will be on VAR duty, assisted by Patrick Hanslbauer.

#2112. West Ham have given Cesar Peixoto a major Wolves headache after Nuno decision

West Ham and Wolves started the Championship season as the two firm favourites for automatic promotion.

Yet, it’s fair to say neither side has hugely impressed in the opening months of the campaign, even if they are both certainly in the hunt to finish in the top two.

Despite their decent positions, the Hammers have seen enough to make a change in the dugout, with Scott Parker replacing Nuno Espírito Santo as head coach.

That shows just how important winning promotion is to the Irons, and Wolves are in a similar boat.

Firstly, it should be said that there’s absolutely no suggestion Peixoto could lose his job, and Wolves will rightly point out that they are ahead of West Ham in the table.

Some will say it’s extremely harsh that Nuno has been sacked with his team just four points away from second, so it would be on another level if Peixoto was dismissed, as Wanderers are third, and just two points behind Swansea going into the midweek fixtures.

Nevertheless, there’s no denying that Peixoto still hasn’t got the backing of all Wolves fans, which is largely down to their inconsistent performances.

There is no clear pattern of play from the Portuguese head coach, and his constant changes to the XI have been baffling.

As well as that, some fans are not happy with his preference for certain players and his substitutions, which is why chants of ‘you don’t know what you’re doing’ were aimed at Peixoto in the recent game against Watford - which Wolves were winning at the time!

The challenge for Peixoto will be to replicate what Nuno did at Molineux by taking the club back to the Premier League.

The circumstances are very different though, so the reality is that even if they do win promotion, Peixoto will not receive the adulation of his former Porto teammate.

Nuno’s appointment at Wolves in 2017 was the start of a remarkable journey for the Midlands outfit, during which time they hit heights that few thought were possible.

As a result, Nuno is viewed as a legend at Molineux, as he built the best team seen in decades, as Wolves returned to the European stage and regularly bloodied the noses of the best clubs in the country.

Plus, he also bought into what the city was about, and he had a special bond with the supporters.

Following on from that, it feels that any Wolves manager since is, perhaps unfairly, compared to Nuno, even if there is an understanding that the ambition of the owners is nowhere near what it once was.

So, with news of his sacking, it’s inevitable that some fans will call for Nuno to return to the place they feel is ‘home’ for the ex-Nottingham Forest chief.

Of course, that won’t be the view of every fan, but Nuno’s departing message in 2021 was that this is ‘not a goodbye, it’s see you soon’, suggesting that he too would be open to returning at some point.

Despite his mixed start to this season with West Ham, Nuno would be seen as a coup for any Championship club, so if Peixoto does struggle at any point, then it’s not hard to imagine that calls for the former manager to return will grow, especially as he is available.

You do have sympathy for Peixoto, because this is none of his doing, and it’s giving him a headache and distraction that he doesn’t need just months into his Wolves career.

Furthermore, it’s not like he is actively disliked by Wolves fans, more that he hasn’t fully won them over, whilst some will be delighted at their league position.

But, rightly or wrongly, Nuno’s availability will naturally add a bit more pressure, and it’s undoubtedly going to be brought up to Peixoto at some point.

Will Wolves and West Ham both win promotion this season? Let us know in the comments below.

However, that doesn’t have to be a bad thing, and, if he embraces the pressure, it will allow him to try and build his own relationship with the supporters.

Ultimately, they both want the same thing - for Wolves to reach the Premier League, and preferably by playing stylish football.

So, instead of Nuno’s shadow lurking in the background negatively, he must use it as motivation to make his own mark at Molineux, even if it’s unlikely he will manage to match his legacy.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

#2110. Jake Cooper interview after Millwall's loss to Birmingham City sparks reaction

Millwall captain Jake Cooper has sparked a reaction through his post-match assessment of the Lions' 3-0 defeat against Birmingham City at St. Andrew's @ Knighthead Park on Tuesday night.

Having romped to a 4-1 success over lowly Derby County on Saturday, there was hope that Alex Neil's side could continue an upsurge in the Championship standings.

Instead, they were the side who found themselves three goals behind in very little time, with all of Birmingham's strikes from Alex Cochrane, Max Bird and Jay Stansfield coming ahead of the half-hour mark.

Blues climbed into the automatic promotion places as a result, with Chris Davies' men winning four of their last five matches, scoring 14 goals during that timeframe.

Having finished third last season, Millwall have started the current campaign indifferently, winning five of their opening 14 encounters, whilst a sixth loss of the campaign saw them drop to 13th.

Cooper, 31, knows the Championship inside out, with his outing on Tuesday taking him nine away from 450 appearances in the division for the Lions and his previous club, Reading.

Although Birmingham found themselves cruising to victory by the time Bird made it 2-0 on 16 minutes, it was Millwall who created the first-half's only 'big chance' whilst the hosts still forged 15 attempts before the interval.

Speaking to Millwall's in-house media post-match, Cooper believed that the scoreline didn't reflect the overall balance of the game.

"Obviously, the first feeling is disappointment, like you say," he said. "I don't think they did enough to score three goals against us.

"I think we had some good opportunities to get back in the game, at important times, that we couldn't take.

"It's important at this level, both boxes are what makes the difference. They were clinical and we, unfortunately, were lacking in that area today," Cooper added.

The summer recruit was key to Blues' fourth win in five Championship games

Davies' side have developed a habit of putting those who visit St. Andrew's to the sword, with it being the third successive home outing in which Birmingham have netted at least three goals.

Millwall only tested Ryan Allsop with two of their 16 attempts, though, which tells its own story by and large, and Cooper's assessment certainly baffled some of the home support.

"My head would be on Mars if we’d got thumped 3-0 and my centre half who were playing the way he did said this," wrote one Blues supporter.

"Funny every team we’ve beat this season say the same thing, yet here we are second in the league, sour grapes" said another Bluenose.

"Commentators last night said "this is a very un-millwall like performance" different commentators said the same on a few occasions and remember it being said on Saturday as well, maybe we just know how to nullify teams and make them look a bit average?," said another.

It has also been claimed that this is a general viewpoint held by teams who have lost in B9, with another verdict reading: "Funny every team we’ve beat this season say the same thing, yet here we are second in the league, sour grapes."

Blues and Millwall fans, what are your thoughts on Jake Cooper's assessment? Comment below

"How can he say Birmingham didn’t do enough to score their 3 goals? It was a joy to watch how fluid Birmingham were. Game was done inside 20 odd mins," backed up the general consensus from Blues fans.

There were also some Millwall fans not on board with Cooper's stance, with one stating: "lol they looked like scoring every attack in that first half. Could have been 5 or 6."

If Birmingham's fans were bemused by Cooper's stance, then the likelihood is they will also have felt the same way when reading Neil's post-match thoughts.

"The fact we have created the chances is a good thing because we looked threatening, but the lack of clinical edge in the final third was a big problem for us," he said.

"Goals change games. The lack of discipline in the first half didn't help us, albeit they have had four shots and three of them go in the back of our net.

"We are really disappointed that we didn't manage to build on the weekend. It is disappointing the manner we have lost the game."

Millwall will look to respond against West Bromwich Albion at The Hawthorns on Saturday, whilst Birmingham host Swansea City.

#2109. Inside Oliver Glasner's Forest struggles: Unserious players who act like superstars when they don't deserve to, alarming physical data - and squad's grumbles revealed

Published: 12:00 EDT, 2 November 2026 | Updated: 05:17 EDT, 3 November 2026

If football management were gambling, Oliver Glasner has just done the equivalent of walking into one of Nottingham’s top casinos and chucking everything on red.

Not satisfied with hammering his Forest players publicly after Saturday’s 2-0 defeat at Brentford, Glasner then had the squad running on the banks of the River Trent for their customary Sunday recovery session. The social media footage has to be seen to be believed – Premier League footballers jogging through an overgrown field, filmed by a baffled dog-walker.

Even if Forest were doing well and their players were easy to manage, these would still be risky moves. Instead, Glasner's side are 19th in the table and he is trying to handle a notoriously restless dressing room.

Forest are believed to pay Glasner more than £10million a year and until now owner Evangelos Marinakis has been patient. But in the Premier League most fans are sceptical when club officials talk about long-term projects and three-year plans. Only three of the current 20 managers have lasted three years in their current job.

Any manager who loses regularly is under pressure, particularly at a club who sacked three managers last season and another in the summer. Glasner has lost six of 10 as Forest boss and won only once. Forget the spin: results alone mean Glasner is under the pump.

If there are no signs of a reaction against Manchester City on Saturday, it promises to be an uncomfortable November international break.

If there are no signs of a Nottingham Forest reaction against Man City on Saturday, it promises to be an uncomfortable November international break for Oliver Glasner

There was not one single moment that broke Glasner’s patience but the 30th minute at Brentford on Saturday probably contributed heavily.

Forest centre back Murillo, who has regressed alarmingly this season, watched idly as Bees goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher launched the ball way over his head and into the path of Dango Ouattara. Ouattara then breezed past Murillo before Nikola Milenkovic turned the cross into his own net. Glasner was unhappy with the shape Murillo was in when he returned for pre-season training and was furious at such slack work.

It was not the first time Forest had been exposed like this, either. Jay Dasilva’s winner for Coventry at the City Ground in September came from a similar diagonal pass from keeper Carl Rushworth, though that time Daniel Munoz – one of Glasner’s pupils – was at fault. Again, slack. Again, sloppy.

Daily Mail Sport understands Glasner does not see enough seriousness in his squad. This group of players get on well but nonetheless, there is a view that poor results do not hurt them enough. Is it really time for laughing and joking around the training ground when you have taken one point from a possible 15?

Most of this squad have never won a European trophy, or one in Europe’s top five leagues. Glasner has three. Some around him believe there are Forest players who carry themselves like superstars when they do not deserve to.

It is thought Glasner is also frustrated with himself. Looking back, perhaps he wishes he had started with a bang, because the 52-year-old was alarmed at the physical data from previous seasons.

In 2024-25, Forest covered fewer kilometres than any other team, and last season only Liverpool and Chelsea covered fewer. In 2024-25, only Arsenal made fewer sprints; last season, only Everton were below Forest. Glasner’s Palace sides were never lower than 12th in those four categories.

When Glasner has been outspoken in the past, it has usually worked. At Wolfsburg and Frankfurt, performances improved. At Crystal Palace last season, Glasner let rip at his bosses after a game at Sunderland last January and most expected him to be sacked. Instead, he left in the summer after delivering the Conference League. The dynamic at Forest is very different though – and Glasner may soon understand why.

Glasner was unhappy with the shape Murillo (left) was in when he returned for pre-season training and was furious at the Brazilian's slack work at Brentford

Player power was a major factor in Ange Postecoglou and Sean Dyche's sackings last season. When players believe they can go above the manager’s head and vent to those in charge, they will. This is the danger for Glasner.

Daily Mail Sport understands there are players who love neither the new style – Glasner is a committed three-at-the-back man and many of the squad feel more comfortable in a back-four – nor the Austrian’s strict approach. He is very different from the avuncular Vitor Pereira, whose easy charm and light-touch approach united the squad post-Dyche and kept Forest in the top flight.

Others are surprised Glasner has not made it a priority to bring the dressing room’s strongest characters onside. Along with Morgan Gibbs-White, both Ola Aina and Callum Hudson-Odoi are powerful voices in the squad and alienating any of them is dangerous. Equally, Ibrahim Sangare and Nico Dominguez are well-respected, and both have been left on the fringes like Aina and Hudson-Odoi.

While Gibbs-White is clearly Forest’s best player, he can be a complex character. If the skipper is not 'having’ a Forest manager, his position becomes vulnerable.

It was a turbulent summer for Gibbs-White, who was frustrated no Champions League club came in for him and ultimately changed agents. He was also left out of England’s World Cup squad. Some believe that Glasner’s rigid tactical framework does not bring the best from Gibbs-White, who likes to roam across the front line and drop deep when he wishes. While Pereira understood this, Glasner does not operate like that.

At times this season, Gibbs-White’s body language has been striking. Team-mates who make mistakes feel his anger but the 26-year-old has only one goal (a penalty) and two assists this term.

Gibbs-White watched team-mate Elliot Anderson leave Forest for City last summer and perhaps questioned why he was not on the same path to the Champions League.

It is tempting to wonder about some of the advice Gibbs-White has received from those around him, though. Because if Gibbs-White is wondering why he is still playing for a bottom-half Premier League club, it is never a bad idea to look in the mirror.

Callum Hudson-Odoi is a powerful voice in the dressing room and Glasner would do well not to isolate him

If  Morgan Gibbs-White is wondering why he is still playing for a bottom-half Premier League club, it is never a bad idea to look in the mirror

Marinakis did not make Glasner the highest-paid manager in Forest’s history just to show him the door at the first sign of trouble. When the pair held talks, Glasner is thought to have stressed the need for time to make his vision work.

Neither man suffers fools and it is easy to imagine that Marinakis would have approved of parts of Glasner’s outburst. That does not give Glasner a free pass, because Marinakis factored in player feeling when dismissing Postecoglou and Dyche.

If the Glasner experiment fails, George Syrianos will come under scrutiny. Forest’s chief football officer has more power at the club than at any other time and he pushed hard for Glasner, whom he has known for some time through links to German football.

It is believed the pair had some contact over possible transfer business during Glasner’s time at Palace, and Glasner would likely have welcomed the chance to work with Syrianos at Selhurst Park.

In December 2023, Syrianos wanted Glasner to replace Steve Cooper but Marinakis chose Nuno Espirito Santo instead. Marinakis’ son, Miltiadis, is at the training ground regularly and will report back to his father. These are testing times for Glasner and his champion.

Dyche has had his say, too. During a poor run of results last season, he gathered the Forest players and staff for their views on what needed to change.

Anticipating their opinions on formations and tactics, Dyche was bewildered when one player queried the decision to move the weekly barber visit from Friday to Thursday. Nevertheless, that player is still at Forest and Dyche lasted less than four months.

Dyche  made many mistakes at Forest but his latest posts on Threads felt relevant.

If the Glasner experiment fails, George Syrianos will come under scrutiny. Forest’s chief football officer has more power at the club than ever before and he pushed hard for Glasner

The problem at Forest is that even if the players fail to stand up and be counted, they are rarely the ones to pay the ultimate price

They read: ‘The badge is bigger than all… and yet it seems not nowadays! I can only hope it turns and the culture we were insisting upon is now being assessed and realised as what was and is needed. Oliver is out there saying what I was saying… in his own style.

‘Nottingham Forest are still finding the goals hard to come by – and I had it along with my staff – we scored but nowhere near what the metrics were telling us, so not enough to stay in our job?

'We had 35 efforts at goal v Wolves and yet a 0-0 result and it culminated in myself and staff being sacked. I hope Oliver is given more time, the fans stay with him and the players stand up and be counted.'

The problem at Forest is that even if the players fail to do so, they are rarely the ones to pay the ultimate price.

Stoke City have made it four away wins on the spin after their 2-1 victory against Blackburn Rovers at Ewood Park on Tuesday evening, as one summer signing stole the show once more.

Stoke continue their ascent up the Championship table with their latest victory away to Blackburn on Tuesday night, as the Potters cement their status as real play-off contenders this year.

Mark Robins' side are flying right now despite a difficult start to the season initially, with just one defeat in their last 11 league games, as summer capture, Jack McGlynn, is receiving his flowers for his contribution to this excellent form.

FLW has consulted AI chatbot ChatGPT to name the best eight owners in the Championship.

Pivotal in their victory at Blackburn on Tuesday was American attacking midfielder McGlynn, whose wide free kick caught everybody to take his goal tally in the Championship this season to four, and giving Stoke the lead in the process.

A mix-up between Yuri Ribeiro and Moussa Baradji at the back in the second half gave the Potters a 2-0 lead, and though Blackburn pulled one back late on, and had an equaliser controversially disallowed for a push on Ben Wilmot, Robins' side held on for all three points once again.

The star of the show against Preston North End the weekend prior, McGlynn is quickly becoming a popular figure at Stoke amongst fans and teammates, as both Wilmot and Viktor Johansson have reacted to his recent post.

Luke Graham said: "Scary good young man."

Certainly, McGlynn is impressing everyone around him right now, including his teammates, and those in the Potteries will be hoping that can only continue.

McGlynn, 23, joined Stoke late in the summer window from MLS side Houston Dynamo for a fee of around $5.5 million (£4 million), including add-ons, and after ten Championship appearances, the American has four goals and two assists already.

#2107. GdS: Why Milan and Inter are expected to bench their most in-form players

Alphadjo Cisse and Carlo Augusto are both expected to start on the bench in tonight’s Derby della Madonnina, despite being among the best players for AC Milan and Inter so far.

For Milan, tonight’s derby is a chance to extend their unbeaten run in the fixture and to decrease the gap in the standings. For Inter, it’s a chance to end the winless run and to truly assert themselves against the Rossoneri, with +10 in sight.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In other words, it’s a very important game and the tactical battle is expected to play an important role in the outcome. Team selection is thus top of mind for Ruben Amorim and Cristian Chivu who, however, are looking to bench a couple of their best players: Cisse and Augusto.

Starting with Cisse, as Gazzetta dello Sport highlights, Amorim’s decision is both tactical and psychological. He fears that there will be too much pressure on the youngster’s shoulders, while the plan is also to play with a 4-4-1-1 that can turn into a 4-3-3 or a 4-2-3-1 depending on the moment.

In that sense, Amorim believes Diego Moreira and Christian Pulisic are better suited to playing out wide than Cisse. More specifically, they arre better suited to playing out wide when not in possession, where Inter will push hard.

Playing with attacking-minded midfielders like Moreira and Pulisic, plus a trequartista like Cisse behind Goncalo Ramos (i.e. a 4-2-3-1), would result in an unbalanced team. Behind Ramos there will be Rabiot, who, when not in possession, will act as a central midfielder.

Therefore, Cisse will start on the bench and be used as needed in the second half.

Moving on to Augusto, over the past two months, he has saved Inter on numerous occasions: the assist that started the comeback against Napoli, the goal in Madrid, the turnaround goal against Bologna, and the decisive blow in the Champions League against Shakhtar.

The latest contribution was the own goal he forced against Venezia, which Chivu’s men used to seal a game that could have gone terribly wrong. Yet, in tonight’s derby against Milan, the Brazilian could start on the bench.

The battle with Federico Dimarco will be decided in the final hours, but the reality is that the Italian is still considered the starter on the left. As such, it’s a question of hierarchy, though we will likely see the player come off the bench either way.

#2106. Celtic B served an unflinching reality in defeat as big-name kids shown no mercy

Ross County boss Stuart Kettlewell reckons his side could have put Celtic's star-studded B team to the sword by an even bigger margin after booking their place in the next round of the KDM Evolution Trophy with a 2-0 win in Dingwall.

The Staggies boss knew his side would face a stern test against a Celtic second string packed with pedigree. £3million summer signing Joel van den Berg was handed his debut, while highly-rated Chelsea youngsters Landon Emenalo and Shim Mheuka also started.

But County proved too strong for their visitors and Kettlewell believes the scoreline flattered the young Hoops after a dominant display in the Highlands.

Speaking to Ross County TV, Kettlewell said: "It was a competitive game. We were a bit frustrated at half-time because we didn't feel we'd handled the ball particularly well and we didn't think we'd quite got our pressing right.

Read more: Celtic handed familiar whistler for Kilmarnock clash as European ref revealed

"We knew Celtic would be comfortable in possession and would look to retain the ball, but we felt there were more opportunities for us to turn it over.

"That said, we scored a brilliant goal in the first half. The run from Dean Cornelius, the cross from Lewis Jamieson and the finish was first class. We were really pleased with that.

"We also had three, four or five other good opportunities, hit the woodwork a couple of times and, despite not playing as well as we would have liked, still created plenty of chances while limiting Celtic to very little.

"I thought we were better in the second half. We won the ball back more often, had a bit more composure in possession and created a lot of opportunities.

"Their young goalkeeper made some outstanding saves and, on another night, we probably score a few more goals. We hit the woodwork again and had numerous efforts on goal.

"You have to give credit to Celtic. They're a young side, but they're a good side. They've brought in players from elsewhere and have talented homegrown players as well. We always knew it would be a good test and another challenge for us to solve in this competition."

Van den Berg's first outing since arriving from PSV offered an early glimpse of the highly-rated Dutch defender, while Chelsea duo Emenalo and Mheuka both got 72 minutes under their belts.

The trio are not part of Celtic's Europa League squad and therefore won't be involved against Besiktas, but they will hope their contributions in Dingwall have strengthened their case for a place in Martin O'Neill's plans ahead of Sunday's Premiership clash with Kilmarnock.

Middlesbrough's Swedish head coach has enjoyed a fine 12-month period at the Riverside Stadium, even if last season ended in heartbreak on two counts.

The style of play at the Riverside Stadium has been completely transformed within said timeframe, and across the opening three months of 2026/27, one man has finally solved the club's biggest achilles heel from last season's final weeks - the ability to score goals.

That is, of course, none other than Will Lankshear, who was one of several high-profile names to have moved to Teesside throughout the summer, doing so from Tottenham Hotspur.

The 21-year-old was no stranger to the Championship at the time of his initial £10m switch from the North London club, but his remarkable adjustment to life at the Riverside could be rewarded with the biggest compliment.

Spurs sold Will Lankshear to Boro in the summer, but, they have clauses written into the contract to protect their position in the future.

The aforementioned deal could still rise as high as £20m with add-ons, meaning Spurs can still benefit financially through their academy graduate's success.

However, right now, no one is benefiting more from Lankshear's goalscoring prowess and all-round game than Hellberg, with his recent double against Charlton Athletic taking the 21-year-old's tally to 13 goals in as many Championship games.

There were concerns over his fitness for Wednesday night's clash at Wrexham, but after being given the all-clear, it has been revealed that a senior England scout will oversee Lankshear's performance on Thomas Tuchel's behalf, with the Three Lions boss set to confirm his latest squad on Friday morning.

Such feats come less than two months after Lankshear marked his Under-21s debut with a goal in the 4-2 win over Kazakhstan at Molineux, further highlighting his remarkable short-term progress.

By mid-October, Lankshear's rapid ascent into double figures was only matched by Manchester City's Erling Haaland, and given his remarkable goalscoring feats, comparisons have already been drawn between him and the 2026 Ballon d'Or winner, Harry Kane, who also began his stellar career in North London.

Dominic Solanke, in fact, has only scored 24 goals in his first 76 appearances for the club, with one of those coming in the current campaign's opening weeks.

It was discussed at length whether Lankshear should have been retained at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium after his 12-goal haul at Oxford United last season, and given the latest set of developments, De Zerbi may be having second thoughts over comments made over the transfer in September.

“Three strikers, how many strikers do you want in the squad? Three strikers I think are enough. To answer about the player in Middlesbrough, no (regrets)."

Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur return from the international break with plenty to prove when they meet at Old Trafford on Saturday.

Michael Carrick’s side have won just once in their last four domestic matches since beating Ipswich 5-2. A Carabao Cup defeat to Brighton was followed by a loss to 10-man Manchester City, before Manchester United drew with Everton and Fulham. Matheus Cunha’s late equaliser at Fulham rescued a point, but Manchester United still sit 12th.

Roberto De Zerbi’s side are bottom of the Premier League with only two points from their opening five games. Spurs have failed to score in four of those matches, while defeats against Aston Villa and Newcastle have added to the pressure.

Michael Carrick has named his starting eleven for the clash at Old Trafford, with Kobbie Mainoo and Youri Tielemans partnering in midfield as United look to get their season back on track.

Senne Lammens starts in goal, with Leny Yoro, Lisandro Martinez, Harry Maguire and Luke Shaw forming the back four. Carrick has opted for Mainoo and Tielemans in the middle, with Amad Diallo, Bruno Fernandes and Matheus Cunha tasked with supporting Bryan Mbeumo up front.

Leny Yoro had a brilliant international break where he made his debut for France. His performance on debut was enough for Zidane to praise the debutant.

Amad, after missing the start of the season with an injury, returns straightaway to the team.

Carlos Baleba starts on the bench and is expected to make his debut today. Marcus Rashford is also on the bench alongside Shea Lacey.

Lammens; Yoro, Martinez, Maguire, Shaw; Mainoo, Tielemans; Amad, Bruno Fernandes, Mbeumo; Cunha.

Mbeumo gets his place through the middle, while Amad and Cunha start on the wing after scoring the late equaliser against Fulham. Fernandes will be expected to start producing the numbers from last season after a lackluster start to the season, except against Ipswich, before the international break.

United need a response after a difficult run, but Tottenham arrive under pressure of their own. With both sides desperate for points, the starting lineups set the stage for an important afternoon at Old Trafford.

#2103. Manchester United player ratings: United failed to win despite advantage

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur returned from the international break with plenty to prove after a disastrous start to the season.

United arrived with just one win, while Tottenham came to Old Trafford without a win.

Both teams had half-chances in the first half but little to show for them. Tottenham had the better chances with chances for Dominic Solanke, Connor Gallagher and Kudus, but none could take advantage of them.

Manchester United came close in the first half to score after Bryan Mbeumo raced towards the goal on a counter-attack to find Amad. He had a difficult shot, and eventually the shot was too weak to cause any damage. The first-half display was met by boos from the Old Trafford crowd at half-time and during the first half as well.

Solanke had another chance at the start of the second half but put it over the top, amid a wrestle with Lisandro Martinez in the six-yard box. It was United, however, who started the second half with promise.

Substitutions by Michael Carrick around the hour mark made the difference as United showed intent before Mbeumo got the goal off Cunha’s low cross. Luke Shaw was at the end of a scuffle with Bentancur, who was shown a red card for headbutting Shaw.

United failed to capitalize on their one-man advantage and seemed to sit on their 1-0 lead, but Solanke punished them with a header to level the game in injury time. The draw left United with just 6 points off their first six games. The result leaves United with their worst start in 40 years.

Lenne Sammens-6          Quiet afternoon for United no.1 till the goal, where he saw the ball go into the back of the net.

Leny Yoro-6       Defensively was fine but offered little upfront. Played out of position, and he showed good defensive awareness on the right back till his substitution.

Youri Tielemans-6          A decent performance and was solid throughout the minutes he was on the field

Bruno Fernandes-5        Another quiet and disappointing evening for the United captain after he failed to impress on a day he needed to get a result for United.

Amad-6              A positive return from injury, showed plenty of promise on the wing but failed to get past a resolute Tottenham side

Matheus Cunha-7           One of the liveliest options for United going forward. Provided an assist to Mbeumo to put United up front

Bryan Mbeumo-7.5        A brilliant finish off Matheus Cunha’s low ball to put United in front. Was dangerous going forward and denied a second on a counter by Kinsky off a brilliant long ball by Baleba.

Diogo Dalot (58’)-6      Provided a decent attacking threat when brought on around the hour mark.

#2102. Shambolic off the park, shambolic on it, dire defeat at Falkirk leaves O'Neill on thin ice

Published: 10:28 EDT, 1 November 2026 | Updated: 15:06 EDT, 3 November 2026

It took Celtic supporters the best part of half an hour on Sunday afternoon to belt out their now traditional rendition of ‘Sack the Board, Sack the Board’.

But as dysfunctional as this club may be off the park, there’s no doubt things are every bit as bad on it. This is an organisation that requires a rebuild from top to bottom. No one should be exempt.

Not the board members, not the management team, not the players. The whole thing is a shambles.

The table will show the champions are right on track to defend their crown. Indeed, the stats here will show this was a contest they dominated. But anyone with a set of eyes and any sort of common sense knows the real story.

Ahead of the match, Martin O’Neill insisted he is essentially oblivious to the outside noise around his team. Aye right.

Callum McGregor looks frustrated as Celtic go down in Falkirk

Scott Tanser celebrates his goal with Falkirk team-mate Owen Eames

Legend at the club though he may be, the Northern Irishman is surely on thin ice. Any other Celtic manager with three wins in his last 10 in all competitions certainly would be.

Frankly, he’s kidding himself on when he says he’s been satisfied with Celtic’s start to the season. The fans aren’t buying that nonsense any more. Does the man himself even believe it?

He continually talks about how his team need time to find their feet. More drivel. We’re now in November. Falkirk also signed 17 in the summer and they seem to be doing relatively well.

The football is just atrocious to watch. It has been all season. Such is the standard of the opposition in Scotland, they usually have just about enough quality to get away with it.

But that’s not a long-term solution to an increasingly worrying problem.

Falkirk, by the way, were outstanding here. They have now won four games on the bounce, each in a thoroughly un-Falkirk way.

Their success under John McGlynn has been built on the ability to pass teams off the park. This victory was far more to do with grit, determination and unity than anything else. Three qualities their opponents are lacking.

Falkirk play like a team. Celtic play like a bunch of individuals. And unless something changes pronto, things are going to get even uglier.

Just as they did in the 2-1 win over Hibernian at Easter Road last week, Celtic fell behind early doors.

Finley Barbrook picked up a loose ball midway inside the visitors’ half before finding Ryan Strain in acres of space on the right-hand side.

The full-back’s cross should have been blootered clear by Cameron Carter-Vickers at the back post with minimal fuss. Goodness knows what he actually tried to do, with the ball simply bouncing off the big American and right into the path of the grateful Ethan Ross, who couldn’t miss from five yards out.

Celtic winger Haissem Hassan gets involved in a scuffle with Falkirk players

Shocking stuff from a Celtic perspective. Carter-Vickers’ comments questioning Celtic’s ‘random’ style following defeats to Rangers in September were bang on the money. But he would do well to examine his own performances too. He’s not as good as some fans seem to think.

It took 10 minutes for Celtic to muster up a response. Liam Scales’ long ball found Camilo Duran in behind the Falkirk defence. His strike across goal from a tight angle beat Scott Bain, but not the far post.

Haissem Hassan’s curler from the follow-up was then brilliantly tipped round the post by the keeper.

Jacob Murrell is the country’s in-form striker with five goals in his last seven outings, but sclaffed a shot wide from the penalty spot at the end of a lovely move involving Owen Eames and Scott Tanser down at the corner flag.

Duran should have levelled things up on the half-hour mark after getting on the end of a wicked Hassan ball into the six-yard box, but headed straight at Bain. Anywhere else but right down the middle would have done the trick.

He was made to pay for that miss as Falkirk doubled their advantage with a wonderful team goal on 38 minutes. Eames was given far too much space on the Falkirk left, but take nothing away from the way he threaded an inch-perfect pass into the path of the underlapping Tanser.

He took one touch to set himself as he drove into the box before coolly slotting past Johnstone. It was the kind of football we’ve become accustomed to seeing on a weekly basis from this side under John McGlynn.

Yes, Celtic looked like they couldn’t even be bothered to try and stop them but that’s not Falkirk’s problem. Their execution was flawless.

Man-of-the-Match Bain was once again called into action as the break came into view, and he once again stepped up, tipping Duran’s left-footed strike from 18 yards around the post.

Martin O'Neill looks on in dismay as Celtic suffer in Falkirk

O’Neill could have taken off any one of his so-called big-name stars at half-time and there would have been no grounds for complaint. He settled for just the one, replacing Callum Osmand with James Forrest.

Osmand should never be playing on the wing anyway. In Yang Hyun-Jun’s absence – and with Jota still searching for fitness – he has had a run of games in that position. You suspect he won’t be holding on to it for long. Square pegs in round holes, and all that.

If O’Neill did give his players a boot up the backside at the interval, you wouldn’t have known it, conceding a shocking third through Murrell within minutes of the restart. Fortunately for the visitors, they got away with it, with VAR spotting that the ball was bundled in by the striker’s hand.

Forrest forced a comfortable stop from Bain on the half-turn, with Callum McGregor then blazing over from a promising position.

The captain has been a shadow of himself all season. In truth, he looks a yard or two off the pace.

For so long, we’ve heard that Celtic just can’t do without him. However, playing like this, he isn’t helping this team.

Bain’s stop to deny Forrest on 68 minutes was simple enough. The one which denied substitute Benjamin Nygren seconds later to seal the points was right out of the top drawer.

The Bairns hadn’t beaten Celtic in 19 years coming into this one. Given the state of this Celtic side, is anyone truly surprised that run has come to a halt?

#2101. Michael Carrick reacts to Man Utd boos after Tottenham draw

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Michael Carrick admitted Manchester United’s 1-1 draw with Tottenham Hotspur was a painful result, after his side failed to protect the lead against 10-man Tottenham at Old Trafford.

Manchester United looked set to claim three points when Bryan Mbeumo scored in the second half off Cunha’s low cross, but Dominic Solanke’s late equaliser in injury time left Carrick facing more questions on United’s performance and his future.

Speaking to BBC Match of the Day, the United manager felt his players improved after the break but failed to handle the situation when victory was within reach.

“It was a mixed game. We found it tough to start with. For a number of reasons, we were not quite there. You could see it was a challenging time,” Carrick said.

“But the lads grew into the game, in the second half I thought we were better in everything. To get the game as we wanted it, in such a good position – we should see it through. We have to manage those situations.”

United have now conceded two late goals that have cost them valuable points, something Carrick believes has made their position look worse than it might have otherwise.

Asked whether a lack of confidence had contributed to United’s slow start, he disagreed but admitted matches can quickly slip away from his side.

The boos at half-time and full-time also clearly affected him.

“It’s not nice, it hurts a lot because I care about this club. But I understand the disappointment, the reality is what it is, we need to get back to winning games.”

#2100. Barry Bannan reacts as Ali Al-Hamadi drops Sheffield Wednesday message

Sheffield Wednesday striker Ali Al-Hamadi has taken to social media to reflect on his start to life at Hillsborough, and team-mate Barry Bannan has reacted to his post.

Al-Hamadi was one of 18 new signings to join Wednesday this summer as part of the club's rebuild under new owner David Storch, but it is fair to say his loan move from Ipswich Town has not gone as well as he would have hoped so far.

It has been an inconsistent start to life back in League One for Wednesday, with the South Yorkshire outfit currently sitting ninth in the table, two points from the play-off places, after winning just two of their last nine league games.

After parting company with Henrik Pedersen last month, the Owls appointed former Stockport County boss Dave Challinor as their new manager this week, and the 51-year-old is set to take charge for the first time in Sunday's FA Cup tie at Oldham Athletic.

However, while Challinor will be keen to run the rule over his new squad over the coming weeks, he may be without Al-Hamadi for the opening games of his tenure after he suffered a fresh injury blow.

Al-Hamadi is yet to open his account for Wednesday since his summer arrival, and injuries have limited him to just eight appearances so far, with his only start coming in the 2-0 defeat to Doncaster last month which proved to be Pedersen's final game.

After missing a few games earlier in the season with a foot problem, Al-Hamadi was not in the squad for Sunday's 1-1 draw with Blackpool due to a new injury, which manager Matt Hamshaw revealed could keep him out for "a number of weeks".

Unfortunately for Al-Hamadi, he has had his fair share of injury woes in recent years, particularly during his loan spell at Luton Town last season, where he scored just one goal and provided one assist in 14 appearances.

Al-Hamadi would have been to get a consistent run of games under his belt at Hillsborough and establish himself in the Wednesday team, but despite finding himself in the treatment room once again, it seems the Iraq international is determined to bounce back from his latest setback.

"Frustratingly, it has been stop-start the last few weeks for me personally," Al-Hamadi wrote on Instagram on Tuesday.

"Working as hard as ever to stay on that pitch, help the team and reach our goals for this season."

Al-Hamadi was inundated with support after his candid reflection on his time at Wednesday, with the post attracting over 16,600 likes at the time of writing, and among those was his Owls team-mate Barry Bannan.

Al-Hamadi has proven himself to be a prolific scorer in the EFL previously during his spell in League Two with AFC Wimbledon, but he has struggled to produce his best form since departing Plough Lane for Ipswich for a fee of just over £1 million almost three years ago.

Despite his injury problems at Luton last season, it is easy to see why Wednesday took a gamble on Al-Hamadi this summer, but as he continues to be plagued by fitness issues, his loan stint at Hillsborough is in danger of turning into another flop.

Should Ali Al-Hamadi be a regular starter for Sheffield Wednesday under Dave Challinor once he returns from injury? Tell us in the comments below!

With Challinor taking over this week, Al-Hamadi would no doubt have been keen to show the new Owls boss what he is capable of, but it appears he will be unavailable for the early stages of his reign, which could allow others to move ahead of him in the pecking order.

#2098. Bryan Mbeumo reacts to Man Utd draw with Tottenham

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Bryan Mbeumo admitted Manchester United have work to do after their frustrating 1-1 draw with Tottenham Hotspur, despite scoring a superb second-half goal at Old Trafford.

The Cameroon international put Manchester United ahead in the 73rd minute, finishing in the far corner after Matheus Cunha created the opportunity from a low cross. However, Dominic Solanke’s stoppage-time equaliser denied Michael Carrick’s side a much-needed victory, even though Tottenham had been reduced to 10 men following Rodrigo Bentancur’s red card.

Manchester United have failed to win any of their last three Premier League games against sides that have received a red card (D1 L2).

3 – Manchester United have failed to win any of their last three Premier League games against sides that have received a red card (D1 L2). Disadvantage? pic.twitter.com/DuSpvymZfu

Speaking to Sky Sports after the game, Mbeumo acknowledged that United had taken too long to find their rhythm.

“We took time to get into the game, but we played well in the second half. In the first half, that wasn’t us, we had to change. We tried to get at them,” he said.

Mbeumo recognised the threat Tottenham posed and admitted the result was disappointing, particularly given United’s position in the game before Solanke’s late goal.

“We know Spurs have good players who can be dangerous. It’s a bit disappointing, we need to work on things.”

United have struggled for consistency in the opening weeks of the season, and dropping points after taking the lead will do little to ease the pressure on Carrick. Mbeumo, however, insisted the team must look ahead rather than dwell on the setback.

“We need to keep going forward, as we have a lot of games.”

Michael Carrick was pleased with Mbeumo’s contribution, highlighting both the quality of his finish and the different roles he has played since joining United.

“Bryan’s done great. It was a fantastic finish again; he’s obviously played different roles for us but we know what he offers,” the United manager said.

“He’s got good quality and obviously the more goals he scores, the better. He’s doing really well for us.”

Mbeumo’s goal was one of the few bright moments in another difficult afternoon for United. Carrick’s team must now find a way to turn things around from here after just six points from six games.

#2097. Gary Neville and Jamie Redknapp tear into Man Utd after Tottenham draw

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United have come under fresh criticism after their disappointing 1-1 draw with Tottenham Hotspur, with Sky Sports pundits Gary Neville and Jamie Redknapp questioning the team’s performance and the challenges facing Michael Carrick.

Manchester United looked on course for a much-needed victory at Old Trafford after Bryan Mbeumo put them ahead in the second half. However, despite Tottenham being reduced to 10 men, Dominic Solanke’s late equaliser denied Carrick’s side all three points.

Gary Neville felt Tottenham deserved the points, pointing to Solanke’s late goal and his impact as Tottenham captain.

“Tottenham deserved a point. That was a really important moment for Solanke. He’d missed some big chances and was captain for the first time,” Neville said on Sky Sports.

“They were the better team by far. If they’d left without a point, it would have been terrible for them.”

The former United defender also expressed concern about what the result means for Carrick, who faces increasing pressure to improve performances and results.

“Michael Carrick is left with a lot to think about. It was a worrying day in terms of the level of performance and a big week ahead.”

Manchester United spent massively in the summer to overhaul their midfield. However, Jamie Redknapp was critical of the performance he saw on the pitch.

“I do not see enough connections in that midfield, and they look devoid of any confidence, ideas, or patterns of play, playing out the back,” Redknapp said.

“Tottenham were just much better than them in every department, but that is a theme this season.”

The former Liverpool midfielder also questioned United’s energy and attacking organization, suggesting the squad is not strong enough to meet the demands placed upon it.

“Their energy levels are not good enough, and they look loose going forward; there was no real structure.”

Redknapp added that Carrick cannot fix every issue alone, insisting the manager needs backing to improve the squad.

“The squad is not good or strong enough, and Michael [Carrick] needs help in that respect.”
